title: Graph, whiteboard, planner and a jungle

items.text: Graph view: your steps as dots you can grab and move around, like Obsidian. Rings show overdue and due-soon steps, and [[step name]] in a note draws a dashed link.
Whiteboard: a corkboard with pinned sticky notes. One per project, plus a general board shared by all projects.
Calendar planner: book steps into a morning, afternoon or evening, on one day or across several. Drag blocks between slots. Missed ones get a suggested free slot you accept in one click.
Library tab: save important links per project, or in a general shelf.
Settings tab: light, dark or system theme, the deadline warning window, project tab order, and your companion.
Project tabs sort themselves by urgency, or drag them into your own order.
Aquarium: a realistic glass cube tank with an air pump, and decorations you can buy with pearls.
Jungle: an alternative to the aquarium, with animals that grow. Pick one in Settings (or turn it off); pearls are shared.

Share & feedback: copy the download link or a ready-made message for friends, and send ideas, bugs or praise as a pre-filled GitHub message. Nothing is sent automatically and no project data is included.
Name your pets: a name box opens when you get a new one, Rename changes it later, and hovering a pet shows its name.
Feeding is hands-on: pets swim over to your mouse, and a click drops food right where you click. The Feed button is now a food bar.
The aquarium and jungle fade out their frame after 3 seconds without the mouse, so they blend into the app. Hover to bring it back (or turn this off in Settings).
Double-click a rendered note to start editing it.
Fixed a case where dragging could get stuck, the toolbar buttons moving under your mouse, and name boxes piling up when adding several steps quickly.
Deadline colours: steps due within 5 days turn orange, overdue ones red. They show on the step, at the top of the project's sidebar, and as a dot on the project tab.
Calendar tab now has an overview of all projects: which one needs attention first, and every deadline across projects in one list. Click one to jump to the step.
You can run several timers at once. Starting a new one no longer stops the others.
Aquarium: the shop now has a Back to tank button, so you can return to your fish.
Project tabs: keep several roadmaps side by side. Double-click a tab to rename it.
Save as… saves the open project to a file you can open anywhere, and Import… adds a project from a file.
Target dates: set a finish day for a step in its notes, or click a day in the Calendar. Overdue steps turn red.
Aquarium: a small pixel fish tank you can drag around. Finish steps and track time to earn pearls, then trade them for rarer fish (up to 7).
This What's new window, shown after each update. Open it any time from the link at the top.
The timer no longer takes space at the top. Hover the ▶ / ■ button next to a step to see the running time.
Click a step to open its notes. They support Markdown and LaTeX math like Obsidian.
Drag any step to reorder it, or use the ↑ / ↓ buttons.
Check for updates button, and the app version next to the name.
+ Add main step for top-level steps, and a small example tree on first run.
Collapse or expand a branch with its chevron; the label now opens notes.
